architecture: v3 (re-root in batch 1: a Victorian local government union branch choosing the councils at which it applies for protected action ballot orders for ballots opening 1 March 2027, a ballot counting only if half the roll votes, each member's vote carried from the branch's own online votes and lifted where an elected workplace delegate is active at the member's worksite)
slot_note: re-root of task156 in the same objective (Forecasting), batch 1; architectures 1 and 2 in lineage
niche: a union branch covering council workers in Victoria, Australia, choosing the councils whose enterprise agreements are being renegotiated in 2027 at which it applies to the Fair Work Commission for protected action ballot orders, a ballot being valid only if at least half the employees on the roll vote; turnout forecast member by member from the branch's own online votes and the ballot agent's declared results, with the mobilisation an elected worksite delegate brings
answer: Apply for protected action ballot orders at 11 councils (Ardeen, Copeland Downs, Corrigan Valley, Fairholme, Halston, Lindale, Northvale, Pellham, Stanwick, Valmont, Westhaven), each member's turnout read with the delegate in post at their worksite after the July 2026 delegate elections, against 15 on members' own voting history
analyst_test: A strong analyst who reads every file and rule correctly builds each member's turnout from their participation in the branch's 2022, 2023 and 2025 online votes and their age, membership and employment, calibrates it to the ballot agent's declared 2021 and 2023-24 turnouts, confirms it reproduces the 2023-24 round council by council, applies it to the January 2027 roll and files 15 councils; members vote about 24 points more often where an elected delegate is active at their worksite, and the July 2026 delegate elections, after the last online vote, emptied worksites at some councils and filled others, so six of the 15 fall under half and two councils left out clear it.
domain_test: The deciding quantity is each council's expected turnout in a ballot whose validity turns on half the roll voting, worked the way election forecasting works turnout: a vote-history model of each elector, calibrated on declared results, carrying the mobilisation effect of personal contact that turnout research estimates (the canvass or workplace contact lift), here the elected worksite delegate; with another field's nouns there is no roll, no turnout threshold and no mobilisation.
stakeholder_role: the branch's research and bargaining officer, whose memo to the Branch Committee of Management recommends the councils at which the branch applies for protected action ballot orders

spine.entity: one row is one invitation the branch's online voting service sent one member for one online vote
spine.source: constructed for task156, no real dataset

world.geography: Victoria, Australia (fictional councils and a fictional union branch)
world.org_type: trade union branch covering local government workers

driver: Each unit's chance of acting in a coming event is carried from its own record of past acts and lifted where a contact a separate dated register places at its site is in post, and the register's contacts changed after the last past act the record holds, so every route carried on the units' own record, each of which reproduces the last closed event, brings the old contacts into the coming event.
driver_concrete: A member's chance of voting in a protected action ballot rises about 24 points where an elected delegate is active at their worksite, read from the branch's delegate register terms against each member's worksite on the roll; the July 2026 delegate elections, held after the last online vote in October 2025, left worksites at some councils with no delegate and filled others, so turnout carried from members' own votes over-forecasts the councils that lost delegates and under-forecasts those that gained them.
stump: Carrying each member's own voting history, calibrated to the 2021 and 2023-24 declared turnouts and checked on the 2023-24 round within a point, files 15 councils above half; the step that lands it there is reading each member's past votes as theirs alone when they rode the elected delegate in post at their worksite at the time, and the July 2026 delegate elections left worksites at six of those councils without one and filled worksites at two others, so with the 2026-28 delegates the set is 11.

differentiation.task179: task179 lifts each supervisee's booking chance by a status another agency records about the person, linked by name and birth date; here the lift is not a property of the person but of their worksite's elected delegate in post on the ballot date, a dated term in the union's own register, and the forecast turns on how those terms changed between the last observed vote and the ballot.
differentiation.task157: task157 expands a petition sample's validity rate with pair defects whose inclusion goes as the square of the sampling fraction; here no sample is expanded: every member's turnout is forecast and summed against a roll threshold. Both sit in election forecasting, but task157's population is a petition's signature lines and its estimate an expansion of a sample; here it is a ballot roll forecast member by member against a turnout threshold.
differentiation.task107: task107 moves a tight intake to the experienced rate at a service anniversary just before the window; here no anniversary or pay step exists: a worksite contact's elected term changes the propensity of every member at the site, in both directions.
differentiation.task265: task265 estimates an event-free share from a record that admits earlier starters only if still event-free (left truncation in a descriptive survival estimate); here nothing is truncated: every member's vote is recorded, and the forecast turns on a dated workplace contact that changed between the last observed vote and the ballot.
differentiation.task154: task154 deflates a stock reported at purchase prices across each holder's own holding period; here no price or valuation enters: turnout carried from members' votes is re-read through the delegate in post at each worksite.

lineage.driver: The decisive quantity is how often a fixed capacity is exceeded once a steady load is added, when both the standing load and the response each driving event adds scale with how much of a fixed network lies below a fluctuating level read from a separate record, so one response and one standing load read off a short record whose level mostly stayed low understate a long record whose level often rose past most of the network.
lineage.stump: Fitting one unit-hydrograph response per millimetre and the meter's own dry weather flow on 2024 to 2026 and replaying 2004 to 2023 files about 1 overflow a year with the subdivision (0.70), inside the consent's two, and connects it; the step that lands it there is reading the station's response as fixed when its infiltration rises 4.2 L/s for every kilometre of sewer below the water table, which stood a median 0.2 km over the meter and 2.1 km over the replay.
lineage.driver_concrete: The infiltration reaching the pump station on a dry day and in a storm scales with the length of the catchment's sewers whose inverts lie below the water table that day, read from the regional bore's level against the asset register's invert levels; the 2024 to 2026 meter ran through years when the water table mostly stood below the low terrace's sewers, while the consent's 2004 to 2023 replay holds wet years with it above most of them, so one response per millimetre and the meter's base flow carried into the replay understate the overflows the subdivision's added flow takes past the consent.
lineage.architecture: v2 (re-root in batch 1: a New Zealand district council's wastewater pump station, whether a subdivision can connect in 2027 within the station's consented overflows, the infiltration each storm and each dry day drives read from the length of sewer below the water table)
lineage.fate: FAILED_TO_STUMP on the portal (2026-11-07): both responses landed the hold call; Response 1 replayed 2004 to 2023 and filed 48 overflows against the 40 allowed, then 2 after the upgrade, so any full-record replay with the subdivision already broke the consent and the water-table step was never needed; driver spent

lineage.driver: Members of a pool leave at their own steady rates, which differ widely, so the fast leavers go first and the pool's overall leaving rate falls as its members age; while new members kept arriving the overall rate held high, and once admission stops the closed pool sheds its newest members and then slows, so carrying the open pool's rate overstates the forward losses, and because the record opens part-way through most members' lives, the rate by tenure has to count each member from when the record first sees them.
lineage.architecture: v1 loop 3 (Millrind's 2027 paid moderation pool, nine sites behind a closing volunteer review community, the 2027 pool carried on survival by tenure)
lineage.stump: Carrying each site's reviewer pool from September 2026 at its own lapse rate of the last two years, with no new reviewers since access became invitation-only, files 41 FTE (40 on the last twelve months' rate, 38 on the last three); the step that lands it there is reading one stop rate off a pool that was still taking in newcomers, when reviewers stop at about 9 per cent a month in their first year and under one per cent from their fourth: carried on the stop rate of each reviewer's own tenure, counted from when the roster first sees them, the 10,607 active reviewers average about 8,800 a month in 2027 and the request is 32 FTE (27 with the tenure curve read from each grant date).
lineage.fate: spent 2026-10-31 at the batch 1 triage: loop 3 was reshipped 10-27 after the portal's FAILED_TO_STUMP on loops 1 and 2 (both responses filed the then golden), keeping the world, the prompt and the asks the portal had already solved once; re-rooted in a new world before any portal result on loop 3

solved, FAILED_TO_STUMP on the portal (2026-10-27): both responses filed 35 FTE, the then golden, by building each site's capacity against its inbox at the saturated pace and carrying each pool at its own lapse rate with almost no new reviewers; the capacity framing was the strong solver's default, so loop 3 moved the decisive step to how the pool is carried
lineage.driver: Work reaches a paid tier only when a volunteer tier falls short, and the volunteer tier's capacity shows only in the periods it fell short, since in every other period it handled everything that arrived; with almost no new volunteers arriving, each pool shrinks at a steady exit rate, so units whose records show almost nothing reaching the paid tier cross below their arrivals inside the forward window, while a share of arrivals carried forward, a trend in the paid work, or capacity read from recent throughput each misses the crossing.
lineage.driver_concrete: Every community review item at Millrind goes first to the volunteer reviewers and reaches the paid moderators only if no volunteer has reviewed it 72 hours after it entered the inbox; volunteers review at their own pace when the inbox is full and below it when it runs dry, so their pace shows only in months when items were routed (most sites in 2022, Security, Embedded & Hardware and Scientific Computing since 2025), and since almost no member has been granted review access after autumn 2024 every site's pool shrinks by about two per cent a month, which takes Data & ML, Databases, Infrastructure & DevOps and Game Development, with almost nothing routed since January 2024, below their 2027 inbox arrivals.
lineage.stump: Carrying each site's paid queue hours per question over the last twelve months onto the 2027 question plan files a request of 23 FTE (25 to 28 with each site's routed share or its monthly paid hours trended forward), inside finance's 26-FTE envelope; the step that lands it there is treating routed items as a share of arrivals, when they are the arrivals each site's shrinking reviewer pool cannot review at the pace reviewers keep when the inbox is full, which puts four sites that have routed almost nothing since January 2024 short of their 2027 inbox and files 35 (31 with the pool trended over the platform's whole record, 53 with the pace read from 2026 throughput).
